title: AI agent memory: architectures, frameworks and trade-offs
thesis: Long-term memory for agents has settled into a few architectures (extracted facts in vector stores, temporal knowledge graphs, OS-style tiered memory) whose trade-off is recall quality versus token cost, and the benchmarks used to compare them are weaker than the marketing.
audience: AI engineers choosing a memory layer for agents in production

questions.question: What types of memory do LLM agents use, and what taxonomies does the research propose?
queries: episodic semantic procedural memory LLM agents

questions.question: How do the main memory frameworks (Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta/MemGPT, A-MEM, LangMem) work and what do they report?
queries: Zep temporal knowledge graph agent memory

questions.question: How is agent memory evaluated (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, others) and how reliable are those benchmarks?
What are the costs: tokens, latency and storage of memory versus long context windows?
queries: long context versus retrieval memory LLM

questions.question: What goes wrong with agent memory in production: forgetting, staleness, contradictions, privacy, poisoning?
